why: `Executor::create` plus a backend selector -- it names the RMW backend the session opens against. rclc/rclcpp have no counterpart because a ROS 2 desktop process selects its middleware with the `RMW_IMPLEMENTATION` environment variable, and an embedded image has no environment to read -- which is precisely how issue 1050 happened: the selector had an env rung and no baked one, so a PX4 module declaring `BACKENDS uorb` could not say so and the registry's first entry won. The hosted env rung (`$NROS_RMW`) still takes precedence, matching `RMW_IMPLEMENTATION`'s authority; this is the rung beneath it. See `cpp:init_with_rmw`, which is the same rung on the free-function surface.
